extracted.intended_audience: legislators, founders of states, political philosophers, and students of political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, establishing, and preserving constitutions and magistracies for city-states (polis), with comparative rules for democracies and oligarchies and practical prescriptions for offices, military composition, revenue, and social policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magistrates: selection and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All the magistrates should be chosen out of all the people; magistrates should be chosen by lot except for offices which require some particular knowledge and skill; no one should be in the same employment twice (or very seldom), and appointments should be limited to a very short time, or at least as many as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sortition for most offices to distribute power broadly; reserve election for technical roles. Short, infrequent terms prevent concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial participation of the people
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole community should be qualified to judge in all causes whatsoever, let the object be ever so extensive, ever so interesting, or of ever so high a nature; as at Athens, where the people at large judge the magistrates when they come out of office, and decide concerning public affairs as well as private contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad popular juries and assemblies serve as checks on magistrates; ensure procedures for holding officials to account at end of term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme power located in assembly with limited magisterial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The supreme power should be in the public assembly; and no magistrate should be allowed any discretionary power but in a few instances, and of no consequence to public business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate ultimate authority in the people’s assembly and restrict executive discretion to minimize abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for civic participation where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: There should, if possible, be a fund to pay all the citizens who have any share in the management of public affairs, either as members of the assembly, judges, and magistrates; but if this cannot be done, at least the magistrates, the judges the senators, and members of the supreme assembly, and also those officers who are obliged to eat at a common table ought to be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensate attendance to secure participation from poorer citizens; if full payment impossible, prioritize officials essential to administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy's foundation: liberty as alternating rule and numerical equality
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation of a democratical state is liberty: one part of liberty is to govern and be governed alternately; according to democratical justice equality is measured by numbers, and not by worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions that allow rotation of offices and treat equality in political power as numerical rather than property-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of life offices
rubrics_metrics.description: In this state no office should be for life; and, if any such should remain after the government has been long changed into a democracy, they should endeavour by degrees to diminish the power; and also elect by lot instead of vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase out lifetime appointments to align with democratic equality; gradually replace entrenched offices with short, lot-selected terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing equality between rich and poor via mixed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a city is made up of two different ranks (rich and poor) establish what is approved by both or the greater part; if opposite, let that be established which shall be approved of by the greater part: but let this be according to the census; e.g., combine counts or divide representation so that the census determines law, and if equal decide by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compromise rules (weighted counts, mixed representation, lot in ties) rather than pure majority or pure property-rule to avoid injustice to either class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of democracy and preferred composition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four kinds of democracies. The best is that composed of husbandmen (tillage/pasturage), next shepherds/herdsmen, and worse are those composed chiefly of mechanics, exchange-men, and hired servants; the worst gives equal share to every citizen without distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer agrarian-majority composition (husbandmen) for stability and civic virtue; avoid overreliance on urban, mercantile, or hired-worker majorities that attend assemblies constantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws to prevent land and wealth concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a democracy of husbandmen some useful laws are: not permit any one to possess more than a certain quantity of land, or within a certain distance from the city; formerly some states forbade sale of original lot and forbade adding to patrimony by usury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit property accumulation near the city and restrict alienation/usury to preserve broad small-holdings and political equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional measures to bind and blend the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute many tribes and fraternities, make religious rites of private persons few and those common, contrive every means to associate and blend the people together and break through former customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use administrative, religious, and social structures (tribes, common rites) to create unity and reduce factionalism; demagogues often exploit expansion of citizenship — limit and regulate such measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for stability over perfection in legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislator and all who would support a democratic government should not make it too perfect but aim only to render it stable; enact laws, written and unwritten, that chiefly tend to preservation and avoid measures that make the form more purely democratic if that undermines duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize durable, practical institutions and avoid reforms that accentuate extremes even if they are 'purer' theoretically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dividing confiscations among the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Demagogues now, to flatter the people, occasion frequent confiscations in the courts; those who have the welfare of the state should enact a law to prevent forfeitures from being divided amongst the people or paid into the treasury, but to have them set apart for sacred uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent perverse incentives for prosecutions by diverting confiscated assets away from popular distribution; deters corrupt prosecutions motivated by gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict frivolous litigation and limit public causes
rubrics_metrics.description: They should take care that the causes which are brought before the public should be as few as possible, and punish with the utmost severity those who rashly brought an action against any one; for the commonalty are often ready to condemn when they gain nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deter vexatious suits to reduce political weaponization of courts and preserve elite confidence in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust assemblies and courts to public revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: When revenues are small there should be but few public assemblies and but few courts of justice: these should have very extensive jurisdictions, but should continue sitting a few days only; when revenues are sufficient, different conduct may be pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale frequency and duration of civic assemblies and courts to fiscal capacity to balance participation costs and ensure attendance by the wealthy when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poverty alleviation as a democratic safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: The true patriot in a democracy ought to take care that the majority of the community are not too poor, for this is the cause of rapacity; save from public money to give the poor enough to purchase a little field or implements of trade, or divide according to tribes if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public resources to create sustainable means for the poor (land, tools) rather than continual cash handouts which breed dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing lot and vote in magistrate selection
rubrics_metrics.description: They have two different ways of electing their magistrates; some are chosen by vote, others by lot; the same may be accomplished if of the same magistrates you choose some by vote, others by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine sortition and election to balance popular participation with selection for competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchy design: opposed principles to democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Every species of oligarchy should be founded on principles diametrically opposite to some species of democracy; the first and best-framed oligarchy is that which approaches a free state with two different census (high and low).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing oligarchic regimes, invert democratic rules appropriately (e.g., emphasize property-rank rather than numerical equality) while preserving stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchy with two censuses and inclusive census rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There ought to be two different census, the one high, the other low: from those who are within the latter the ordinary officers of the state ought to be chosen; from the former the supreme magistrates: nor should any one be excluded from a part of the administration who was within the census; the commonalty included in it should by means thereof be superior to those who have no share in the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tiered property/census qualifications to structure access to offices while allowing some upward mobility for those within lower census.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military composition should align with regime aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the nature of the country admits a great number of horse, there a powerful oligarchy may be easily established (horsemen costly); where troops are chiefly heavy-armed, an oligarchy inferior in power may be established; light-armed and sailors always contribute to support a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recruitment and military structure mindful of social composition: heavy cavalry favors wealthy elites; light infantry and sailors empower popular classes; mix forces properly to prevent insurrection advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and division of magistracies by city size and tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: In small states the magistrates should be few; in a large one, many: know well what offices may be joined together, and what ought to be separated. First establish regulators in markets, public and private edifices, highways, harbours, and other branches each with appropriate officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor number and specialization of offices to population and complexity; create distinct inspectors for markets, buildings, harbours, roads, lands, and woods as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial officers and audits
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be officers appointed to receive the public revenue and to deliver it out to those who are in the different departments of the state (receivers or quaestors); since some magistrates have business with the public money, there should be other officers whose employment should be nothing else than to take an account of what they have, and correct any mismanagement therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate treasury/receiving functions from auditing and oversight; create dedicated accountants/auditors to prevent embezzlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of sentencing and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: One person should often have the custody of the prisoner's body, while another sees the sentence against him executed (as the eleven did at Athens): for by so much the less odium attends those who carry the laws into execution... for the same persons to pass the sentence and to execute it will subject them to general hatred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate judicial decision-makers from execution officers to avoid concentration of odium and potential abuses; distribute unpleasant duties among different offices and younger citizens where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make execution-related offices non-permanent and properly incentivized
rubrics_metrics.description: The office to take care that sentence is executed upon those who are condemned is very disagreeable on account of the odium attending it, so that no one will engage therein without it is made very profitable, or, if they do, will they be willing to execute it according to law; therefore it ought by no means to be a separate office from others, nor should it be continually allotted to any individuals, but the young men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid permanent stigmatized offices; rotate unpleasant tasks, provide compensation or combine with other duties to attract capable actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military and high magistrates: public benefaction to secure favor
rubrics_metrics.description: Over military magistrates there are sometimes more officers; those who enter high office should make magnificent sacrifices and erect some public structure, that the people partaking of the entertainment, and seeing the city ornamented with votive gifts, may see with pleasure the stability of the government; the nobles will have their generosity recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage elites to spend on public benefactions and ceremonies to display commitment to the common good and secure popular esteem (but beware of mere greed masquerading as generosity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious offices and sacred revenue management
rubrics_metrics.description: There are persons whose business is confined to religion; as the priests, and those who are to take care of the temples, or officers of the sacred revenue. Next to these are those appointed to have the general care of public sacrifices which the laws do not entrust to the priests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and institutionalize religious administrative roles and protect sacred revenues from secular capture; assign clear responsibilities for temples and public cults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special offices for social and cultural administration in leisured states
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate states peculiarly happy and having leisure require particular magistrates for themselves: governors of the women, officers to see laws executed, those who take care of the boys and preside over their education, those who have the care of gymnastic exercises, theatres, and every other public spectacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prosperous polities, create specialized magistracies for family, education, and civic culture to maintain social order and civic training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regime-appropriate guardianship institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three magistrates to whom some states entrust the supreme power; namely, guardians of the laws, preadvisers, and senators; guardians of the laws suit best to an aristocracy, preadvisers to an oligarchy, and a senate to a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match high-level constitutional organs to regime type: rule-of-law guardians for aristocracy, advisory preadvisers for oligarchy, representative senate for democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit expansion of citizenship and demagogue tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who have taken the lead in such a democracy have endeavoured to support it, and make the people powerful by collecting together as many persons as they could and giving them their freedom, not only legitimately but naturally born, and also if either of their parents were citizens; they ought, however, to take care, and do this no longer than the common people are superior to the nobles, and then stop; for, if they proceed still further, they will make the state disorderly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict radical expansion of political privileges used by demagogues; extend citizenship cautiously and stop once balance is at risk to avoid disorder and elite backlash.
